| #385 | 2026-08-18 | **N66 ROOT-CAUSED AND FIXED — the OS-follow theme path was UNREACHABLE CODE. N65 triaged at source; the silent failure is closed and instrumented.** C#-only batch: no component, no shell, no string change. **N66 — the mechanism, proven against the MAUI source, not guessed.** `App.xaml.cs:112-113` pinned `Current.UserAppTheme` to a concrete value at boot, and the first line of the OS-flip handler itself (`Current.UserAppTheme = a.RequestedTheme;`) pinned it again. MAUI resolves `Application.RequestedTheme` to `UserAppTheme` whenever that is not `Unspecified`, and `TriggerThemeChangedActual` drops the event when the resolved value does not change (`if (_themeChangedFiring \|\| newTheme == _lastAppTheme) return;` — dotnet/maui `Application.cs`). **So the handler disabled itself the first time it ran.** Everything it does — the `SpixiThemeName` re-bake, `setEdgeToEdge`, `reloadAllPages`, and with it the #315 parked-Account dispose — has been dead since the boot event. That is exactly why ONLY the System path was broken while explicit Light/Dark stayed correct: the pick path never needed this event. **The fix keeps `UserAppTheme` Unspecified for the whole session** (= "follow the platform", which is what System means), so `ThemeManager` must no longer read the automatic theme off `UserAppTheme` — the new `isPlatformDark()` reads `Application.Current?.RequestedTheme`, at both sites. Without that half the fix would have resolved EVERY automatic theme to light: a harder break than the bug. **The revived handler is gated on `automatic` and returns early** — it is newly reachable at any moment, and under an explicit pick an OS flip must not reload every page for a theme the user does not see (the #242 round-2 flicker lesson). `reloadAllPages` was hardened for the same reason: null `MainPage`, a page that is not a `SpixiContentPage`, and a throwing reload no longer take the OS theme change (or the later pages) with them. **N65 — triaged, and the silent failure closed.** Verified at source: all 13 language files parse clean (no BOM, no duplicate key, no separator-less line), so `loadLanguage("pt-br")` cannot return false for a parse reason, and `de-de` demonstrably loads on Windows. Two real defects found on the way and fixed: the parse-failure branch returned false **with no log line at all**, and a DUPLICATE key would make `Dictionary.Add` **throw out of `loadLanguage`, through the WebView `Navigating` handler that calls it**, leaking the open stream and skipping even the `else`. Both are now caught, named (file + line) and reported. `SettingsPage` logs the request, the load result and the code that ended up active — the one line that separates "the load failed" from "the load worked and the four surfaces disagree". **NOT fixed, deliberately: the four-way split.** It needs that log line from a device first (#215). Protocol in `docs/n65-triage-language-pick.md`. ⚠ **Honest residual on N66:** the Windows sibling (panes disagree) follows from this mechanism directly. The **Android** leg (Account stays light under system-dark) does NOT follow from it by itself — no shell reacts to a live OS flip, because no stylesheet carries `prefers-color-scheme` and no page reloads. If it survives this fix, the next step is the parked-instance/`data-theme` inspection on device, not more code. **★ Opus review round: 1 MAJOR + 5 MINOR + 5 NIT; 1 MAJOR and 6 lesser findings LANDED.** **MAJOR-1 was mine, and it was the cost of un-deadening the path:** `reloadAllPages` walks the whole `NavigationStack`, and `MiniAppPage` is on it. It is the ONE page that assigns `_webView` directly instead of calling `loadPage`, so `loadedHtmlFileName` stays null and `reload()` falls through to a raw `_webView.Reload()` of the mini-app's own entry point. A `chat` message's payload is `Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(str)` — raw text, no envelope — so there is nowhere to put a reference without either a Core change or smuggling it into the message body, which would render as visible junk on any client that does not strip it. **What the read DID find is the shape of the fix, and it is small.** ① `msgReaction` is the exact precedent: `ReactionMessage(msg_id, reaction)` already carries "a reference to another message" through the same pipe, via a typed payload registered in `SpixiMessageObjectMap`. ② `SpixiMessageCode.chatStream` (53) ALREADY has a typed payload — `ChatStreamMessage(MessageId, Message, Sequence, IsStream)` — so the natural change is one appended field there, not a new message code. ③ Its parser reads a fixed sequence and never validates that it consumed the buffer, so **trailing bytes are ignored**: an old client receiving a reply degrades to a plain message rather than failing. ④ Persistence is a well-worn path — `FriendMessage`'s deserializer is explicitly append-tolerant (`if (m.Position < m.Length)`), which is how `transactionId`, `reactions`, `sent`, `errorSending` and `sequence` were each added. **The FE belief is also wrong in the other direction:** un-gating is NOT a one-line cap flip. The COMPONENTS are built (quote bubble, composer context strip, menu Reply — #79/#25), but `chat.html` never wires them: it sets `reply: bridge.cap('reply')` and the handler branch is marked "never reached in v1". That is a BE ask with a design in it instead of a question | 🟡 → BE / protocol run (N57); nothing built |

Payload is provably the same value — SettingsPage pushes the Account address from `getPrimaryAddress().ToString()` (:143), the exact expression HomePage shares — and the native rung is gated on the shell's address matching that push, so a caller passing anything else falls to the clipboard rather than silently sharing something different. ⚠ **The smoke pin asserted the bug.** "The no-navigator.share engine still reaches the same fallback" was green for the whole life of the defect.
